title: Qwen Custom HTTP and Spark Local Compute contract
productBoundary: A Qwen chat can be a Custom HTTP bot. A Spark Local Compute machine is a separate execution host, not a provider, vendor, custom bot, or Usage ring. Their identities, credentials, and accounting never merge.

qwen38.match: Exact Qwen 3.8 family names, including Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8; Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-80B are not matches.
qwen38.truthRule: The approved model id, outbound request model, response model when supplied, transcript stamp, and usage row must agree; mismatch or silent fallback fails.

scopedMcp.allowlist: Missing includeTools preserves legacy all-tools access; an explicit empty list exposes none; a populated list exposes only exact selected tools.
scopedMcp.transportBoundary: Restricted tool subsets are supported for Custom HTTP. ACP vendors that cannot enforce the subset fail closed.
scopedMcp.secrets: MCP environment values stay in the encrypted credential store and are absent from ordinary state, probe errors, support exports, and child ambient environment.
scopedMcp.platforms: macOS and Windows use the same saved contract; Windows .cmd and .bat shims use the shell while native executables launch directly.
scopedMcp.liveProof: The selected Qwen model must call one allowlisted read-only local MCP fixture, receive its marker, and return the exact final marker within two model requests.

localCompute.identity: A host and its advertised profileId or capability never become a Workhorse provider, custom bot, or model row.
localCompute.configuration: Persist only safe endpoint metadata, explicit desk/external-runtime/worker/auditor capability grants, exact continuation grants, and an absolute token-file reference. HTTPS is required except loopback HTTP; the token is never copied into state or Link.
localCompute.discovery: Only healthy, role-granted live capabilities appear in workhorse_capabilities and tools/list. Empty grants expose nothing; generic invoke requires a complete typed invocation contract.
localCompute.invocation: Jobs are asynchronous and use strict protocol 1.0 identity, route, hop, artifact role/cardinality/media, typed output, and closed constraint validation.
localCompute.artifacts: Transfers verify declared size and SHA-256 before atomic cache commit; JSON carries artifact references rather than binary payloads.
localCompute.replay: Successful semantic request fingerprints survive restart; an identical idempotency key replays and a changed payload conflicts.
localCompute.offline: A known job whose host is unavailable reports Unknown with timestamped last-observed state and removes stale continuations.
localCompute.continuation: Only an installed and exactly capability/tool-granted continuation may stage verified artifacts and create one visible Workhorse worker; retries replay that worker.
localCompute.usage: Local Compute execution creates no vendor or Usage ring and cannot be attributed to the Qwen Custom HTTP connection.

usage.connection: A Custom HTTP bot named Spark retains one connection ring; this is not the Spark Local Compute host.
usage.models: Each Qwen or other approved model retains a separate model row beneath that connection.
usage.tokens: Only OpenAI-compatible response usage is booked; missing usage remains unknown.
usage.leftover: Local model capacity is unknown unless the connection has a separate authoritative meter; Workhorse never invents a percentage.
